Izmayil New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Izmail, Ukraine

Not demolished. Established in the 1970s, this cemetery received many pre-WWII gravestones (the earliest from the 1920s) relocated from Izmail's older cemetery, per a 2014 JOWBR survey; it remains operational today. Izmail's Jewish community is first mentioned in the 16th century; population reached 549 (6%) by 1827 and 1,105 by 1847, with a synagogue built 1825. Rabbi Yom-Tov-Lipa Landa served from 1864-1872. A Jewish hospital opened in 1869, and a Talmud Torah for poor families operated 1872-1888; a devastating 1872 pogrom burned 60 Jewish houses. Population reached 2,780 (12%) by 1897 and 4,348 (12%) by 1910; a further 1905 pogrom killed about 50 Jews. Under Romanian rule, Jewish kindergartens, a Tarbut school, and a hospital operated, with Zionist organizations active from 1927. Population fell to 1,326 (7%) by 1930; Soviet authorities deported wealthy Izmail Jews to Bolhrad in 1940-41. German-Romanian occupation from July 19, 1941 murdered 120 Jews immediately; the surviving 52, swelled to nearly 1,000 by Bessarabian refugees, were confined to a ghetto before October 1941 deportation to Transnistria, where most perished. Population reached 1,500 (3%) by 1959; a Jewish religious community was founded in the 1990s.
